title: Concept 33. Tool Execution Failure
summary: Tool execution failure happens when an agent selects the correct tool and provides valid arguments, but the tool fails while executing.

sections.title: 1. What is tool execution failure?
sections.body:
Tool execution failure happens when an agent selects the correct tool and provides valid arguments, but the tool fails while executing.

The problem may be inside the external API, network, database, authentication layer or tool implementation.

### Visual explanation

User request

↓

Correct tool selected

↓

Valid arguments generated

↓

External API execution

↓

**Tool execution fails**

API unavailable / timeout / database error

scenario.title: Scenario — Concept 33. Tool Execution Failure
scenario.situation: Your AI assistant calls a customer management API. python customer = get_customer(customer_id="C101") The arguments are valid, but the API returns: text 503 Service Unavailable The tool execution fails because the external service is unavailable. The agent should not automatically assume that the customer doesn't exist.

choices.label: Ignore it and ship anyway
choices.explanation: Skipping detection leaves users exposed and makes root-cause analysis harder later.

choices.label: Add detection signals first
choices.explanation: Instrument logs, metrics, and traces that reveal this failure mode.

choices.label: Apply a production fix / mitigation
choices.explanation: Apply layered mitigations, validate with tests, and monitor recovery.

sections.title: 2. Why does it happen?
sections.body:
- API outage.
- Network failure.
- DNS resolution error.
- Authentication failure.
- Authorization failure.
- API rate limits.
- Database unavailable.
- Connection timeout.
- Tool implementation bug.
- External service response errors.

sections.title: 3. Where does it happen?
sections.body:
- REST API tools.
- MCP servers.
- Database tools.
- Browser automation.
- File-processing tools.
- Cloud services.
- Payment integrations.
- Internal enterprise systems.

sections.title: 4. Real-time example
sections.body:
Your AI assistant calls a customer management API.

```python
customer = get_customer(customer_id="C101")
```

The arguments are valid, but the API returns:

```text
503 Service Unavailable
```

The tool execution fails because the external service is unavailable.

The agent should not automatically assume that the customer doesn't exist.

sections.title: 5. How to detect it?
sections.body:
Monitor:

| Signal | Possible failure |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP 401 | Authentication |
| HTTP 403 | Authorization |
| HTTP 429 | Rate limiting or quota |
| HTTP 500 | Server error |
| HTTP 502 | Upstream gateway failure |
| HTTP 503 | Service unavailable |
| HTTP 504 | Gateway timeout |
| ConnectionError | Network failure |
| TimeoutError | Execution timeout |

The exact meaning of provider-specific errors should be checked in the response body and API documentation.

sections.title: 6. How to fix it?

diagram.title: Visual flow — 6. How to fix it?

steps.label: Solution 1 — Retry transient failures
steps.narration: Solution 1 — Retry transient failures Use bounded retries with exponential backoff and jitter.

steps.label: Solution 2 — Timeout management
steps.narration: Solution 2 — Timeout management Every external tool call should have a suitable timeout.

steps.label: Solution 3 — Circuit breaker
steps.narration: Solution 3 — Circuit breaker Temporarily stop sending requests to an unhealthy dependency.

steps.label: Solution 4 — Authentication refresh
steps.narration: Solution 4 — Authentication refresh Refresh expired credentials where supported.

steps.label: Solution 5 — Fallback
steps.narration: Solution 5 — Fallback Use an approved alternative service when appropriate.

steps.label: Solution 6 — Error classification
steps.narration: Solution 6 — Error classification Return structured errors instead of exposing raw exception messages to the LLM.
